title: Roadmap Launch Readiness / Incident Review - Eng & Product Sync

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-18
Start Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Liam, Sofia, David, Priya, Ethan, Alex
Link to notes: https://confluence.redwood/product/launch-readiness-2025-09-18 (shared deck)

Summary: quick recap at top; we had a pilot in us-west-2 for Dedicated where p95 spiked to ~1.2s for text gen when sequence length > 1024; possible KV cache invalidation and batching regression after last runtime patch.

[00:00] Liam: ok, let's kick off. thanks everyone for hopping on. main agenda: roadmap, the incident from the pilot, and what we need to ship for launch readiness. sofia, do you want to run through the incident timeline?

[00:18] Sofia: yeah, sure. so timeline, we rolled the runtime patch last thursday night, 11pm PST, it's the one that changed the continuous-batching logic and a small change to the kv-cache sharding. initial canary looked fine, but after we ramped to ~150 concurrent reqs the p95 started creeping up, and by friday morning it was consistently above 1 second.

[00:40] David: to add, we saw repeated cache misses where the kv cache entries weren't being reused for certain prefix shapes. I'm calling it the "K-V cash" issue in the logs which made me laugh, but basically the TTLs were being reset on some evictions. so more cold starts.

[01:05] Alex: hmm, are we sure it's the TTL and not the kernel selection change? the runtime also changed some attention kernel heuristics. it might interact with sequence length distribution. we saw it mostly when length > 900 tokens.

[01:30] Sofia: good point. our hypothesis is combined: the kernel selection increased per-token CPU in some paths, which increased latency, which then frustrated the batching and evicted some cache entries because of timing. the cache thrashed.

[01:58] Priya: from ops side, we saw alert noise. pagerduty fired twice between 3 and 4am as the ramp happened. customers on the pilot reported timeouts, we triaged and rolled back the patch at 04:30.

[02:15] Liam: okay rollback bought us stability, but we need a fix before we reattempt the Dedicated rollout. what's the remediation story?

[02:25] David: immediate fix is to apply stricter cache pinning for known hot prefixes and revert the TTL tweak; medium term, add observability into the kv hit/miss ratio per-request-id. i sketched an epic with metrics and a dashboard.

[02:48] Ethan: QA reproduced locally, if you replay the production trace we saw the same 1.1s p95 on the patched runtime. i put the replay trace in the ticket, but the reproduction required exact batching timing which is fiddly.

[03:12] Sofia: ok so action item: pairing session between runtime and infra folks to get deterministic repro; alex can you take point?

[03:22] Alex: yep will do. propose we instrument a lightweight sampling of kv keys so we can correlate misses with kernel path.

[03:40] Liam: also important: canary telemetry. i want a single-pane view that shows p50/p95, kv hit rate, batch size distribution, and tail CPU. we should also surface sequence length histogram.

[03:58] Priya: i created a draft dashboard, link in chat. it tags by region and by model variant so we can see if a quantized variant is behaving differently. quick note: SSO sign-off from security is pending, so we can't go GA until that's done.

[04:20] David: perf note: when cache thrash happens we also see a lot of small allocations in the runtime process which causes GC pauses in the python shim. might be worth profiling.

[04:40] Ethan: QA suggestion: add a noisy-traffic profile to the load bench to surface these GC/noise interactions. currently our bench is a clean steady state.

[04:55] Liam: agreed. priya, can you coordinate that with QA and infra?

[05:00] Priya: yes i'll coordinate. i'll include a schedule for the bench next week and invite all owners.

[05:10] Sofia: on backlog prioritization, we have two candidate fixes: 1) quick TTL revert + cache pinning (low risk), 2) rework kernel heuristic to avoid the heavy path for lengths <1k (higher risk). recommendation: do 1 now, schedule 2 for next sprint.

[05:35] Alex: i support that. 2 requires regression testing across GPUs and might delay launch.

[05:45] Liam: ok that means we defer the streaming-batching UX polish and keep the core runtime fixes in sprint. let's record that decision.

[06:00] Sofia: on release mechanics can we do a staggered canary in three steps: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with monitoring gates at each step? if kv hit rate drops below 85% or p95 > 700ms we halt.

[06:20] David: i can wire those gates into the canary controller. just need the exact thresholds and the alerting rules.

[06:30] Priya: also we need comms plan for customers on pilot; liam you'll send the postmortem and plan?

[06:38] Liam: yes i'll draft the postmortem and include timeline and next steps.

[06:45] Ethan: QA will run the noisy bench on staging Wednesday and share results. i'll add scenarios for length distribution and batching jitter.

[06:58] Alex: i'll prepare the rollback playbook and test it in staging so it's practiced.

[07:10] Sofia: one more risk: if we reapply the patch and see thrash again, we need to be prepared to autoscale more aggressively. but that adds cost. trade-off: uptime vs cost. we should document when to scale vs rollback.

[07:30] David: agreed; i'll add a scaling policy draft and tie it to the canary gates.

[07:45] Priya: any blockers from security? we still need SSO cert rotation docs and KMS activity log sign-off.

[07:55] Liam: i'll follow up with security. sounds like not blocker for the immediate fix but GA timeline depends on completion.

[08:10] Sofia: quick note on metrics: please ensure the telemetry doesn't sample away rare keys; we need full coverage for a short window to debug.

[08:28] David: yes will flip sampling to full for 2 hours during canary redeploy.

[08:40] Liam: great. let's recap outcomes: immediate fix (ttl revert + pin hot prefixes), pair session to reproduce, noisy load bench next week, canary with gates, rollback playbook, postmortem to execs. defer noncritical UX work.

[09:00] Priya: i'll update launch checklist and send calendar invites.

[09:12] Liam: any other items? hearing none, thanks everyone. adjourn.

Transcript notes: transcription contains minor errors (product names, acronyms sometimes mis-transcribed e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "es-el-oh" for SLO). Refs to artifacts: incident ticket #INC-2025-472 (in tracker), playbook draft at https://docs.redwood/internal/playbooks/rollback-dedicated, dashboard draft at https://grafana.redwood/d/launch-readiness.
